subject: science
title: Health and disease: germs and the body
instruction: Work through the chapter one step at a time.

activity.instruction: Tap each glowing circle to see which disease attacks that part of the body.
activity.intro: Germs that cause disease attack different parts of the body. Tap each part to find out which.

hotspots.label: Nose and throat: common cold
hotspots.text: The common cold is caused by rhinoviruses. They infect the nose and the airways, but not the lungs. It spreads through droplets from coughs and sneezes, and through shared objects.

hotspots.label: Lungs: pneumonia
hotspots.text: Pneumonia is caused by bacteria such as Streptococcus pneumoniae. The tiny air sacs of the lungs (alveoli) fill with fluid, so breathing becomes hard.

hotspots.label: Liver and blood: malaria
hotspots.text: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, a protozoan. It multiplies first in the liver, then inside red blood cells, which burst.

hotspots.label: Intestine: typhoid, amoebiasis, roundworm
hotspots.text: Three diseases start in the intestine: typhoid (the bacterium Salmonella typhi), amoebiasis (the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica) and ascariasis (the roundworm Ascaris). All three spread through contaminated food or water.

hotspots.label: Legs: filariasis
hotspots.text: Filarial worms (Wuchereria) live in the lymph vessels, often of the legs. Over years, the limbs can swell a lot, which is why it is also called elephantiasis.

hotspots.label: Skin: ringworm
hotspots.text: Ringworm is caused by fungi, not worms. It makes dry, scaly, itchy rings on the skin. Heat and moisture help it grow.

activity.doneText: You found where each disease strikes!

activity.instruction: Move each disease into the group of germ that causes it.
activity.intro: Diseases are caused by different kinds of germs. Sort each disease into its group.

items.say: Typhoid is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi.
The common cold is caused by rhinoviruses.
Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium.
Amoebiasis is caused by the protozoan Entamoeba histolytica.
Ascariasis is caused by the roundworm Ascaris.
Filariasis is caused by filarial worms.

activity.doneText: Every disease is in the right group!

activity.instruction: Move each disease onto the way it spreads.
activity.intro: Knowing how a disease spreads tells us how to stop it.

pairs.text: Bite of a female Anopheles mosquito

pairs: Malaria spreads through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

pairs.text: Bite of a female Culex mosquito

pairs: Filariasis spreads through the bite of a female Culex mosquito.
The cold virus spreads through droplets in the air.
Typhoid spreads through food and water contaminated by the germ.
Ringworm spreads by touching infected skin or sharing towels and combs.
activity.doneText: Now you know how to break the chain!

activity.instruction: Put the life cycle of the malaria parasite in order. Start with the bite.
activity.intro: The malaria parasite needs two hosts: a human and a mosquito. Put its journey in order.

items.text: Mosquito bites, parasites enter the blood
items.say: An infected female Anopheles bites and injects the parasite, as sporozoites.
The sporozoites travel to the liver and multiply there.
The parasites attack red blood cells, which burst and release haemozoin. This causes chills and high fever.

items.text: Sexual stages form in the blood
items.say: Some parasites become gametocytes, the sexual stages, inside red blood cells.
A female Anopheles bites the sick person and takes up the gametocytes.
They fuse and develop in the mosquito's gut. New sporozoites move to its salivary glands, ready for the next bite.

activity.doneText: You followed the parasite through both hosts!

activity.instruction: Tap the best answer. Read why after each question.
activity.intro: Time for a quick quiz on this chapter.

questions.q: A doctor asks for a Widal test. Which disease is being checked?
questions.explain: The Widal test confirms typhoid, which is caused by Salmonella typhi.
Plasmodium causes malaria. The Anopheles mosquito only carries it from person to person.
The common cold is caused by a virus. Antibiotics work against bacteria, not viruses.

questions.assertion: In malaria, the high fever and chills come back every few days.
questions.reason: Red blood cells burst together and release a toxic substance called haemozoin.
questions.explain: Both are true. Each round of bursting red blood cells releases haemozoin, which brings back the fever.
Despite its name, ringworm is a fungal infection of the skin, nails or scalp.

questions.q: Which part of the body does pneumonia mainly affect?
options: The air sacs of the lungs
questions.explain: In pneumonia, the alveoli of the lungs fill with fluid, which makes breathing difficult.

questions.q: Which step best prevents both malaria and filariasis?
questions.explain: Both are spread by mosquitoes, so removing stagnant water and using nets cuts both diseases.

questions.q: Filariasis can cause long-term swelling of the legs.
questions.explain: The worms block the lymph vessels, so fluid builds up and the limbs swell over the years.
